title: 500 flat class rules vs 500 descendant-combinator rules
variable: flat class selectors vs descendant-combinator selectors
claim: perf-lint.ts lists 'Deep/BEM-vs-nested CSS selector cost' among the patterns it deliberately cannot check, because Gameface does not expose authored selector text through CSSStyleSheet.rules/cssRules - so the guidance to flatten selectors currently rests on engine docs alone with nothing measured behind it. This case is the number, and per the spec it is also what quantifies the value of a selector-flattening tool before that tool is built.
result: Styles 1.10x at 30, 100 AND 300 elements (unrounded: 1.1023, 1.1018, 1.1027) - a flat ~10% style-time penalty that does not grow with element count. In absolute terms at 300 elements that is 0.633ms -> 0.698ms of styling per frame, against a 31ms frame. IMPLICATION FOR THE SELECTOR-FLATTENING TOOL: the spec says this case exists to quantify that tool's value before it is built, so plainly - this is weak support for building it. The measured saving is ~0.065ms per frame at 300 churning elements, roughly 0.2% of a 31ms frame budget, and it does not worsen at scale. The consistency across a 10x range is the strongest part of the result: the cost is real and reproducible, just small. A tool justified on these numbers would be justified on maintainability, not performance. Two caveats before treating this as final: it was measured at 500 rules with a two-ancestor chain, and both are parameters a real project could exceed.
notes: Applicability gate: DIRECT. Descendant combinators and class selectors are standard and supported; classList was verified manually against the Player. Rule 1: one variable, the selector form. Every rule body is byte-identical between A and B and the colours are generated from the same function, so the two variants render the same pixels. Rule 2: identical DOM - both build the same #root > .lvl1 > .lvl2 > .tile structure, so B's ancestor chain exists in A too and is simply not referenced by A's selectors. Rule 3: identical JS, byte-for-byte. Rule 4: no text, no assets. Rule 5: 300 tiles occupy 1852x1032 inside 1920x1080. Rule 6: the class churn IS the case and replaces the shared damage driver; every tile gains or loses .hot every frame from load, which is what forces re-matching against the full rule set. Rule 7: colours and positions derive from the index only. Rule 8: counts 30/100/300 elements, against a rule count fixed at 500 as the spec specifies. Rule 9: plain HTML/CSS/JS - the rules are literal CSS text, not injected, because runtime CSS-in-JS is prohibited in Gameface and CSSStyleSheet rule access is unavailable. Rule 10: expected axis is Styles. DIFF SIZE EXCEPTION: AUTHORING.md asks for a diff small enough to check by eye, and this one is 500 lines. That is unavoidable here because the rule set IS the variable. It stays reviewable because the change is completely uniform - every line gains the same '#root .lvl1 .lvl2 ' prefix and nothing else differs, which 'diff A.html B.html' shows at a glance.
